### Avoiding the Comparison Trap
Author: Kia Stephens
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/encouragement/encouragement-for-today-may-10-2021.html
Passage: Genesis 30:1
Points:
- Fixating on another person's blessings can quickly breed envy, bitterness, and desperate demands.
- Rachel allowed comparison with Leah to dictate her emotions and rob her of joy.
- Outward appearances hide internal struggles, as Leah suffered from an unloved marriage despite having sons.
- Fixing our eyes on Christ breaks the comparison trap and anchors our identity in God's sovereign plan.

### Sons for Rachel
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/sons-rachel
Passage: Genesis 30:7-8
Points:
- Rachel's envy over her infertility drove her to demand children from Jacob instead of seeking God in prayer.
- Rather than waiting on the Lord in faith, Rachel took matters into her own hands by giving Bilhah to Jacob.
- Rachel named Bilhah's sons Dan and Naphtali to mark vindication and rivalry against her sister.
- God works sovereignly through imperfect and dysfunctional families to advance His redemptive purposes.
- Believers should repent of sinful motives and trust God's grace rather than competing with others.
